acceptance: Owner records Theseus App login/integration ID, allowed repositories, required-check source binding, attesters and gated main branch; these match consumer-configured identities.
Environment protection and workflow separation demonstrably prevent fork/candidate builds from accessing App, tailnet and publisher secrets; no secret value is captured in tracker evidence.
Named Theseus tailnet identity and activation procedure are ready but not activated against shared gateway before observation disposition.
Owner records completed settings/secret administration and explicit approval for the later first live gate.
context: Owner-only administrative boundary. Stop with exact requested owner operation if not authorized/available; ordinary repository implementation permission is not authority to change secrets or hosted settings.
description:
Owner-controlled setup for Theseus PR governance, not reuse of benchbox-oracle. Define the distinct Theseus App login and integration ID, installations, attesters, required-check source binding, secret-bearing environment and least-privilege token permissions. Provision a named Theseus tailnet identity/client credential, but do not add a shared gateway client or execute live reviews until observation disposition and the first-live-gate item permit activation.
Decision gate: owner must approve and perform App, branch-protection, environment, secret and tailnet administration that agents cannot authorize or access. Record public identifiers, settings evidence and validation results only; never secret values. No App key in a wheel, release build, PR artifact, log or candidate workflow; no secrets:inherit across an untrusted boundary.
Guardrails: BenchBox App, settings, gateway and credential caches stay unchanged. No weakening required checks or bootstrap stand-ins. Missing owner credentials/settings permission is a blocker, not a fallback to BenchBox identity.
